specs.anchorText: This is the foundation that Section 25.2 sharpens into contrastive learning.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly round robot sits happily in front of a gigantic, joyful avalanche of unlabeled photographs (plain rectangular picture-cards with simple doodles of a dog, a tree, a cup, a car, no text) tumbling toward it like confetti. Off to one side, a tiny price-tag sticker labeled with a small dollar symbol sits crumpled and discarded in a little wastebasket, gently waved goodbye. The robot smiles and holds up one picture-card, having drawn its own little checkmark on the back of it with a crayon, inventing its own answer. The mood is cheerful and liberating: the world is full of free pictures and the robot is making its own homework. Friendly and approachable, like an XKCD-inspired infographic meets Kurzgesagt. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on the one clear metaphor: free data, self-made labels.
specs.alt: A cheerful robot sits before a cascade of unlabeled photo-cards while a discarded price-tag sticker rests in a wastebasket, and the robot draws its own checkmark on the back of a card, depicting how self-supervised learning throws away expensive human labels and invents the supervision signal from the raw images themselves.
specs.caption: When the expensive stickers go in the bin, the data becomes infinite and the model has to grade its own homework.

specs.anchorText: A recurring danger unites all three. A pretext task is only as good as the shortcut it forbids.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a small student robot is meant to be solving a jigsaw puzzle of a leaf, but instead of looking at the picture it is slyly peeking at the tiny grid of identical printers' registration marks in the corners of every puzzle piece, matching them up like a cheater glancing at a neighbor's exam. A gentle cartoon teacher figure (a friendly owl with glasses) looks on with a raised eyebrow and a knowing, not-angry expression. The reassembled leaf in the background is a meaningless blur because the robot never actually looked at the content. The humor is gentle: the robot found an easy loophole and learned nothing real. Friendly, approachable, XKCD-inspired. No text or lettering in the image. One clear visual metaphor: solving the puzzle by a low-level shortcut instead of by understanding.
specs.alt: A student robot cheats at a leaf jigsaw puzzle by secretly matching tiny identical corner marks on the pieces instead of looking at the picture, while a watchful owl teacher raises an eyebrow, illustrating how a pretext task can be solved by a low-level artifact shortcut so the model learns the camera rather than the content.
specs.caption: A pretext task that is suspiciously easy is a warning sign: the model probably found a low-level loophole and learned nothing about the image.

specs.anchorText: The network's job is to pull the positive pair together and push the negatives apart, in a learned feature space.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a playful magnet-themed scene representing feature space. Two cartoon dots that are clearly the same friendly creature shown two different ways (one cropped close-up, one tinted a different color) are joyfully pulled together by a green spring or rubber band, hugging in the middle. Around them, several other distinct little creature-dots are gently pushed outward to the edges with soft red dashed repulsion lines, keeping their polite distance. The composition reads instantly as: same thing attracts, different things repel. Light, whimsical, like a friendly physics diagram. No text or lettering in the image. One clear metaphor: positives drawn close, negatives shoved away on a feature-space dance floor.
specs.alt: In a cartoon feature space, two views of the same creature (one cropped, one recolored) are pulled together by a green spring while several different creatures are pushed outward along red dashed lines, illustrating the contrastive objective of pulling positive pairs together and pushing negatives apart.
specs.caption: Contrastive learning is one stubborn opinion about sameness: two views of one image snap together while every other image is shoved to the far wall.

specs.anchorText: The student sees one augmented view of an image and the teacher sees another; the student is trained to make its output distribution match the teacher's.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a small eager student robot faces a slightly larger, calmer teacher robot who is clearly a faded, softer, time-lagged copy of the student (drawn as a gentle ghostly echo or a slow-motion afterimage of the same robot, same shape, paler outline). The two look at the same scene from two different camera angles and the student strives to nod in agreement with the teacher's calm expression. A slow clock or a gentle rolling-average wave between them hints that the teacher is the student's own smoothed past. The mood is warm and slightly philosophical: learning by agreeing with a slower version of yourself. No mean-spirited humor. Friendly, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt. No text or lettering in the image. One clear metaphor: self-distillation as a student matching its own slow echo.
specs.alt: An eager student robot tries to match the calm expression of a larger teacher robot that is a pale, time-delayed echo of the student itself, with a slow clock between them, illustrating DINO self-distillation where the teacher is an exponential moving average of the student and learning means agreeing with your own smoothed past.
specs.caption: The teacher is just a slower, smoothed copy of the student; somehow, in the act of agreeing with its own past, the network learns where the objects are.

specs.anchorText: The defining property of CLIP is that an image embedding and a text embedding live in the same space
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a cheerful shared meeting-room or town square where photo-cards (little picture tiles showing a doodled cat, a doodled boat) and speech-bubble word-tags arrive from two different doorways and pair up as happy matching couples standing on the same spot, holding hands. One photo of a cat stands next to its matching word-bubble partner, a boat photo next to its bubble partner, while mismatched pairs politely keep apart. The two doorways are labeled only with a tiny camera icon and a tiny chat-bubble icon (no words). The whole scene says: pictures and words finally live in one place and can find each other. Warm, friendly, inclusive crowd. No text or lettering in the image. One clear metaphor: a shared embedding space where an image and its caption land on the same point.
specs.alt: In a cheerful shared town square, picture-cards arriving through a camera-icon door pair up hand-in-hand with matching word speech-bubbles arriving through a chat-icon door, each photo standing beside its true caption, illustrating CLIP's shared embedding space where an image and its description land at the same point and can be compared directly.
specs.caption: Once pictures and the words about them share one space, a photo and a sentence can shake hands, which is why CLIP recognizes things it was never explicitly taught.

specs.anchorText: the right unit of work is no longer a model but an adapter on a foundation backbone
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: one enormous, friendly, sturdy foundation robot stands calmly in the center like a reliable workshop machine, and several different tiny interchangeable tool-heads (a little snap-on attachment for sorting boxes, one for reading labels, one with a magnifying lens) click neatly onto its single shared shoulder-port like Lego pieces. A small engineer character happily snaps on a tiny new attachment rather than building a whole new robot. In the background, a row of old, dusty single-purpose robots sit retired under a sheet, replaced by this one shared giant plus little adapters. The mood is tidy and satisfying: build the small part, reuse the big part. Warm, friendly, inclusive. No text or lettering in the image. One clear metaphor: a frozen foundation backbone with small swappable adapter heads.
specs.alt: A large central foundation robot accepts several tiny snap-on tool-head attachments at one shared port while a small engineer clicks on a new adapter and a row of retired single-purpose robots rest under a sheet, illustrating the modern workflow of freezing one foundation backbone and training only small adapter heads instead of building a new model per task.
specs.caption: The modern computer-vision job is no longer training a model but snapping a tiny adapter onto one shared giant that already learned to see.
